what_is_carbon.title: Understanding Carbon Credits & Market Dynamics
what_is_carbon.subtitle: An educational guide on carbon units, compliance versus voluntary markets, and the drivers of credit quality.
what_is_carbon.sec1_title: What Does 1 Carbon Credit Actually Represent?
what_is_carbon.sec1_p1: A single carbon credit is a measurable, verifiable instrument representing the reduction, avoidance, or durable removal of exactly one metric tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent (1 tCO2e) from the Earth's atmosphere.
what_is_carbon.sec1_p2: Carbon credits allow farmers who sequester soil carbon, forest stewards protecting biodiversity, and technological removal facilities to monetize their ecological contributions.
what_is_carbon.sec2_title: Voluntary Carbon Markets (VCM) vs. Compliance Systems
what_is_carbon.sec2_vcm_desc: Driven by corporations and individuals fulfilling voluntary climate targets (e.g. Science Based Targets initiative, Net-Zero pledges). Prices vary widely from $5 to $600+ based on permanence and verification quality.
what_is_carbon.sec2_compliance_desc: Legally binding government caps where high-emitting power plants, factories, and airlines are mandated to surrender allowances. Governed by strict statutory rules with penalties exceeding €100/tCO2e for non-compliance.
what_is_carbon.sec3_title: Why Does Quality Vary So Dramatically?
what_is_carbon.factor1_desc: The guarantee that the carbon sequestration would NOT have occurred without the financial incentive provided by carbon credit revenue.
what_is_carbon.factor2_desc: Durable geological mineralization (DAC/Biochar) locks carbon for millennia, whereas forestry projects face wildfire and logging reversal risks.
what_is_carbon.factor3_desc: Modern digital MRV (Satellite remote sensing + IoT ground soil probes) prevents inflated historic baseline calculations.
what_is_carbon.factor4_desc: Projects that improve rural farmer livelihoods, preserve endangered species, and restore water tables earn high quality premiums.

greenwashing.title: Combating Greenwashing in Carbon Markets
greenwashing.subtitle: How Bhoomi Carbon deploys two completely independent verification pillars to eliminate deceptive offsets.
greenwashing.p1_desc: Issuing credits for forests that were never at risk of deforestation, or legacy renewable grid projects that were already financially viable.
greenwashing.p2_desc: Selling the exact same metric tonne of avoided emissions to multiple corporate buyers across overlapping voluntary and national registries.
greenwashing.p3_desc: Packaging unverified, temporary soil or tree plantings as equivalent to 1,000-year permanent geological removals.
greenwashing.dual_defense_desc: We do not rely on a single score. Our engine runs two distinct, non-overlapping verification layers:
greenwashing.engine1_title: Pillar 1: Transparent ICVCM Rule-Based Quality Scoring
greenwashing.engine1_desc: Deterministic, public scoring rules grounded in the Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market (ICVCM). Standard registry verification awards +2 points, while legacy unverified methodologies receive severe penalties.
greenwashing.engine2_desc: An independent Machine Learning Isolation Forest model trained on global registry transactions. It evaluates multivariate patterns across vintage, credits volume, project type, and registry distribution without human bias.
greenwashing.distinct_highlight_desc: A predatory project could theoretically falsify paperwork to pass traditional rule checks. However, if an unverified registry claims an abnormal issuance of 2,000,000 credits for a 2017 vintage, the Isolation Forest immediately flags it as a Statistical Anomaly. Neither system alone provides complete security.

pricing_explained.title: Transparent Carbon Credit Pricing Formula
pricing_explained.subtitle: Discover the exact mathematics behind quality multipliers, baseline benchmark indices, and fair value ranges.
pricing_explained.formula_text: Fair Price ($/tCO2e) = Benchmark Price × Quality Multiplier
pricing_explained.formula_desc: Benchmark prices are derived from regional ICVCM category reference trades. The Quality Multiplier is mathematically mapped from the project's holistic ICVCM rule evaluation.
pricing_explained.example_case1_title: Example A: Unverified Legacy REDD+ Project
pricing_explained.example_case1_desc: Baseline Benchmark: $28.00 | Vintage: 2017 (>5 yrs old, -1) | Registry: Unverified (-2) | Storage: Biological (-1) | Quality Score: 32 (Red Badge) | Multiplier: 0.45x
pricing_explained.example_case1_calc: Fair Price = $28.00 × 0.45 = $12.60/tCO2e (Significant quality markdown protects buyers)
pricing_explained.example_case2_title: Example B: Certified Durable Biochar / DAC Project
pricing_explained.example_case2_desc: Baseline Benchmark: $140.00 | Vintage: 2024 (+1) | Registry: Puro.earth Verified (+2) | Storage: Durable Mineralization (+1) | Quality Score: 95 (Green Badge) | Multiplier: 1.22x
pricing_explained.example_case2_calc: Fair Price = $140.00 × 1.22 = $170.80/tCO2e (Premium pricing rewards high-integrity climate developers)
pricing_explained.rule_verified_reg: Verified Standard Registry (Verra, Gold Standard, Puro.earth, ACR)
pricing_explained.rule_verified_reg_why: Rigorous accredited third-party validation & public serial retirement.
pricing_explained.rule_unverified_reg_why: High risk of phantom emissions reductions and lack of audit trail.
pricing_explained.rule_renewable_legacy: Legacy Renewable Energy / Solar Grid Methodology
pricing_explained.rule_renewable_legacy_why: Renewable electricity is now grid-competitive and lacks additionality.
pricing_explained.rule_old_vintage_why: Older vintage credits reflect historic baselines and excess dormant inventory.
pricing_explained.rule_forestry_risk_why: Subject to biological reversal risks (wildfire, pestilence, logging).
pricing_explained.rule_permanent_bonus_why: Permanent geological and mineral carbon removal lasting > 1,000 years.
